title: Africa and Latin America

cards.b:
Africa and Latin America are the heart of the 'Global South' that India claims to speak for. They offer markets, resources (oil, gold, lithium, pulses), votes at the UN, and a field of competition with China.

In the past decade India has opened new embassies, offered large lines of credit and brought the African Union into the G20 (2023). Yet its trade with these regions is still small compared with China's.

UPSC asks about the Africa partnership (IAFS, Kampala Principles), Latin America (trade, lithium, Brazil) and a comparison with China. Look for patterns: demand-driven, capacity building, development partnership.

India's early role was moral and political. It led the UN campaign against apartheid: it banned trade with South Africa in 1946, and cut diplomatic ties in 1954. It backed independence for Ghana, Kenya, Namibia and Zimbabwe. It sent peacekeepers to Congo.

About three million people of Indian origin live in Africa, mainly in South Africa, Mauritius, Kenya and Tanzania. The diaspora is both an asset and, at times (Uganda 1972), a burden.

cards.h: The modern partnership: IAFS and the Kampala Principles
cards.b:
• India–Africa Forum Summit (IAFS): I (New Delhi, 2008), II (Addis Ababa, 2011), III (New Delhi, October 2015) with leaders from all 54 African countries; India announced $10 billion in concessional credit and $600 million in grants.
  • Pan-African e-Network (2009): tele-education and tele-medicine.
  • Kampala Principles (July 2018): in Uganda's Parliament Modi set out ten guiding principles: Africa's priorities come first, demand-driven partnership, local capacity building, no conditionality, and so on.
  • IAFS-IV: planned for New Delhi on 28–31 May 2026, but postponed on 21 May 2026 because of an Ebola outbreak. As of November 2026 no new date had been announced.

The African Union became a permanent G20 member at the 2023 Delhi summit.

• Lines of credit: over $12 billion across many projects.
  • Trade: about $100 billion a year (Africa as a whole). India is among the top partners. Cumulative Indian investment is estimated near $70 billion.
  • Capacity building: the ITEC programme, scholarships, the Pan-African e-Network.
  • Health: low-cost medicines, Covid vaccines (Vaccine Maitri), the Cheetah project with Namibia (2022) and South Africa.
  • Energy and food: ONGC in Mozambique's gas, pulses imported from Africa, solar power through the ISA.
  • Defence and security: training, anti-piracy patrols, Africa-India Field Training Exercise (AFINDEX), Indian troops in UN missions in Congo and South Sudan.
  • Digital: UPI and Aadhaar-like systems.

India opened a number of new missions in Africa in recent years.

China is Africa's biggest trade partner (about $280 billion a year, as of recent years) and a major lender through the Belt and Road. It has a naval base in Djibouti (2017) and has largely removed tariffs on African goods.

India cannot match China's money. It stresses instead:

  • Democratic values and a shared colonial history.
  • Low-cost, human-centred projects (health, skills, IT).
  • Fewer strings and less debt risk, in contrast with the 'debt-trap' charge against China.
  • Partnerships with Japan (Asia-Africa Growth Corridor, 2017) and the EU.

Critics say Indian projects are slow, and credit lines are often delayed. India's trade with Africa is also skewed: oil and gold imports, with exports of pharma, vehicles and machines.

• Trade: about $50 billion. India imports crude oil (Brazil, Venezuela, Colombia, Guyana), gold, and vegetable oils; it exports vehicles, pharma, chemicals and IT.
  • Brazil: a partner in BRICS, IBSA and G4. Modi made a state visit in July 2025 after the Rio BRICS summit.
  • Argentina and Chile: lithium. India's KABIL signed deals for lithium blocks in Argentina (2024). A Chile–India PTA exists (2006), widened in 2017.
  • Mercosur–India PTA in force since 2009.
  • Guyana: Modi's visit in November 2024 was the first by an Indian PM in over 50 years. Guyana's new oil is of interest to India.
  • Mexico, Cuba, Caribbean: trade, vaccines and the CARICOM link.

In July 2025 Modi toured Ghana, Trinidad and Tobago, Argentina, Brazil and Namibia in one trip, a sign of the Global South focus.

cards.h: Institutions that tie India to both regions
cards.b:
IBSA (2003)

India, Brazil, South Africa. Brasilia Declaration, 2003. A democratic, multicultural South–South forum with a small development fund (the IBSA Fund).

BRICS

Brazil and South Africa are members. Egypt and Ethiopia joined in 2024. India chaired in 2026.

G4 and the UN

Brazil is in the G4. Many African and Latin American states back UN reform.

Others

The G20, G77, WTO coalitions, the International Solar Alliance and the Global Biofuels Alliance (with Brazil, 2023).

Realists see India competing with China for influence and resources. Liberals stress mutual gains and institutions. Post-colonial writers ask whether India repeats extractive patterns. India says its model is demand-driven, Africa-led, and without conditions.

The 2026 Ebola-related postponement of IAFS-IV shows how health shocks can slow even a prestige event. The key test is whether summit promises become projects.

• Hold IAFS-IV once health conditions allow, with project lists and timelines.
  • Improve credit-line delivery and set up faster project agencies.
  • Build supply chains: critical minerals (lithium, cobalt), pulses and edible oils.
  • Strengthen digital and pharma partnerships, regional manufacturing and vaccine production in Africa.
  • Use shipping and naval presence to guard sea lines to Africa.

Make one point with a number: AU in the G20 (2023), Kampala Principles (2018), $10 billion (2015), IAFS-IV postponed (2026).

"Discuss the significance of Africa to India's foreign policy." (typical)
"India's engagement with Latin America: opportunities and constraints." (typical)
"Compare India's and China's approach to Africa." (typical)

Structure: (1) historical ties; (2) IAFS and Kampala Principles; (3) offers: credit, capacity building, health, energy; (4) Latin America: trade, lithium, Brazil; (5) China comparison; (6) problems; (7) way forward.

quiz.q: The Kampala Principles were announced by Modi in:
How many African leaders/countries took part in IAFS-III (2015)?
quiz.w: IAFS-III invited all 54 AU member states, with 41 heads of state or government attending.

quiz.q: India cut diplomatic ties with South Africa in:
The African Union became a permanent G20 member at the summit in:
quiz.w: At the New Delhi G20 Summit, September 2023.

quiz.q: The IBSA grouping was set up through the:
India's KABIL signed lithium-block deals in 2024 with:
quiz.w: KABIL (Khanij Bidesh India Ltd) signed for lithium exploration blocks in Catamarca, Argentina.

quiz.q: IAFS-IV, planned for May 2026 in New Delhi, was postponed because of:
quiz.w: The AU and India announced the postponement on 21 May 2026.

quiz.q: The Asia-Africa Growth Corridor was conceived by India and:
quiz.w: It was announced in 2017 at the AfDB meeting in Gandhinagar.
The Pan-African e-Network project began in 2009.

quiz.q: The Mercosur–India PTA entered into force in:
quiz.w: It came into force in June 2009.
